evidence.title: Copilot access reduced completion time among task completers in an early controlled study
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: Peng and colleagues report randomizing 95 recruited professional developers to a JavaScript HTTP-server task with or without Copilot access. Conditional on completing the task, mean completion time was 55.8% lower with access (reported 95% interval: 21%–89%). The seven-percentage-point success-rate difference was not statistically significant. Five treated participants did not complete tool setup. Observation context: May–June 2022.

source_locations.SRC-151: Experimental design; Results, paragraphs following Figure 6; Discussion; arXiv submission history

evidence.limitations: One standardized task, recruited population, and early Copilot version. The time estimate conditions on completion, rather than all randomized developers; it is not a universal productivity gain. Tests checked task correctness, not security or broader code quality. Paper wording about completer count is ambiguous; no count is inferred. This is not a matched replication of METR.
evidence.open_questions: Which results transfer to other populations, tool versions, longer periods and operational governance settings? No such transfer is established by inclusion.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: A bounded example of reduced completion time, alongside a non-significant success-rate difference.

terms.name: Constraint compression
terms.definition: A reduction, often AI-enabled, in the practical barriers of knowledge, expertise, labor, cost, time, or coordination that once limited an activity. It describes the change in constraints, not the eventual impact of the activity.

relationships.explanation: Commons interpretation: A bounded example of reduced completion time, alongside a non-significant success-rate difference. This describes a bounded application, not validation or general prevalence.

These studies used different developer populations, tasks, tools and periods. A completion-time benefit in Peng does not reverse or replicate the METR mature-repository slowdown; retain both settings and their limitations.
